Second, an emissions burden, or "macroscale", analysis considered the total emissions within the primary air quality impact area. This area was delineated as the transportation impact area; that is, the area bounded by Memorial Drive, Massachusetts Avenue, Portland Street, Cambridge Street, McGrath and Monsignor O'Brien Highways and Cambridge Parkway. Third, a regional VMT analysis compared the Kendall Square location with a location of a similar project at a suburban site or at another urban site with either more parking or less potnetial for public transportation use. (Please note that EPA found that air impacts were adequately addressed.)
Metropolitan Area Planning Council (July 29, 1977)
HUD acknowledges receipt of the Council's review and its finding that the proposed project, as presented and analyzed in the report, would be consistent with regional goals and objectives.
Boston Redevelopment Authority (August 16, 1977)
HUD acknowledges receipt of the Authority's review and its comment, in general, that its review of the transportation section of the impact statement indicates that the proposed development should not have a significant adverse impact on the streets in theCity of Boston. Regarding the point that a more detailed analysis of regional impact should be performed, we believe that sufficient information was provided with regard to the impact of the "18,500 daily trips." [See pages II-5-67 and II-5-68 of the report.]
Regarding the nonadjustment for traffic returning to preferred Boston routes and for Tech Square trips that may be double—counted, this nonadjustment resulted in the estimated 18,500 and the associated potential regional impacts. These conservation tively high volumes were estimated for the purpose of evaluating the street system within the project area itself. They were then used to discuss qualitatively the regional impacts. A detailed quantitative regional study would demonstrate that the regional problems which were referred to, relate to conditions and areas other than Kendall Square.
Cambridge Redevelopment Authority
Comment noted regarding the publication in newspaper of availability of DEIS for public review and comment.
